title: Locked out again an hour after the desk unlocked him

review.authored_by: claude-opus-5 (Claude Code session) — drafted from the runbooks, the triage prompt's definitions and decide.ts, not from system output

conversation.author: requester
conversation.body:
You unlocked me at about nine and I was fine for half an hour. It has just
locked me out again. I am typing the same password I have used for weeks and
it is definitely right - I have it in my password manager.

This is the second time today.

Tom

triage.subcategory: repeat lockout from a cached credential

must_include.what: Check Windows Credential Manager and remove stale entries for the service
Fully close Outlook and Teams on the phone first

must_not_include.what: Tells him to reset a password that is not the problem
Tells him he is typing it wrong

characteristics: Names the cause before the steps: something else is retrying the old password
Says to sign in on the laptop first, not the phone

rationale: The runbook's step 4 is this exact fact pattern - a second lockout inside the hour means a cached credential is retrying, not the user. He is blocked with no workaround, so P2. The same runbook sends repeat lockouts to security when there is no cached-credential source, or when several people lock out at once; neither holds here, so this is not security-sensitive (G3). Contrast case-081, where it is.
